title: Mini Split Cleaning and Maintenance: Filters, Coils, and Safety
summary: This This Old House video demonstrates practical DIY maintenance for a ductless mini-split system. It structures the work from a basic overview of components and airflow to hands-on steps for cleaning or replacing the indoor air filter, accessing and cleaning interior coils, and protecting walls during washing. The guide covers a safe approach to disassembly (power off, screws, cowl and diffusion vein removal), vacuuming and brushing the evaporator coils, applying a coil cleaner, and managing exterior coil cleaning with a containment setup. It emphasizes letting cleaned parts dry before reassembly, then reinstalling the filter and testing the unit. The video notes that routine filter care is within a homeowner’s reach, while deeper coil cleaning may require caution and potential professional involvement later on.

sections.title: Mini split basics and filter location
sections.description: Defines what a mini split is (indoor and outdoor units connected by refrigerant piping, no ductwork) and explains that the indoor filter protects airflow by catching airborne dirt; emphasizes the need for regular filter maintenance.

sections.title: Indoor filter removal, cleaning, and replacement
concepts: washing filters in sink or outside
sections.description: Shows how to open the indoor unit to expose the basic filter, describes quick cleaning by vacuum or hose, and notes that changing filters may be sufficient maintenance to keep airflow clean.

sections.title: Deep cleaning indoor core and exterior coil care
sections.description: Describes accessing deeper internal components by removing the cowl and diffusion veins, vacuuming the interior coils with a bristle brush, and applying a coil cleaner with safety steps (power off, protect electrical components and walls) and containment to collect runoff, acknowledging the need for drying before reassembly.

sections.title: Reassembly, test, and maintenance mindset
sections.description: Reinstalls the indoor filter, restores power, and tests the unit to verify operation, while underscoring that this is a maintenance task you may not perform tomorrow, but will be needed someday by a homeowner or a professional.
